issues.failure_explanation: The proof's displayed bound is claimed for every |z| >= rho_0 and mu = 0,...,m+1. It carries a decaying factor |z|^{-mu}, which is wrong for derivatives. For real z = t -> infinity, d/dz H_0^{(1)}(kz) = -k H_1^{(1)}(kz) has size ~ k(kt)^{-1/2}. The stated bound gives (kt)^{-1/2} t^{-1}, so it fails by a factor ~ k t. The correct bound has a polynomial or k-power factor instead. The proposition only needs the exponential factor, because Im z ~ sigma-bar on the reflected terms, so polynomial losses are absorbed. But the inequality as written is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the bound by the correct one, with a factor like (1+|z|)^mu or k^mu in place of |z|^{-mu}. Absorb the polynomial factor into the exponential decay in the proof.
issues.overall_effect: The cited Hankel estimate is wrong as stated. The exponential smallness of reflected terms still holds once polynomial factors are allowed, so only the written bound is affected.
issues.title: Differentiated Hankel bound with factor |z|^{-mu} is false for large |z|
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the stated inequality leaves the proposition and all its uses intact, since the exponential factor dominates any polynomial.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of the lemma treats E_sigma, which has kernel R_{sigma,N} minus the localized nearest-image part, as a Y_R -> Y_R operator with norm O(P e^{-c_1 sigma-bar}). Proposition 4.1 only gives kernel smallness for observation points in a compact K or source points in a compact subarc Gamma_R^int. The paper's own remark says it yields no operator-norm bound on all of Gamma_R x Gamma_R. E_sigma contains (1 - chi_im(x)chi_im(y)) times the nearest-image kernel. This is small only if chi_im equals 1 near the vertical boundaries, which is never stipulated: only 0 <= chi_im <= 1 and the support are specified. Without it the leftover kernel is O(1) near the endpoints.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require chi_im = 1 on a fixed neighbourhood of the vertical boundaries. Then prove directly that the kernel of E_sigma, including the endpoint region, is C^m-exponentially small on the whole Gamma_R x Gamma_R and gives an exponentially small H^{1/2} operator norm.
issues.overall_effect: The step needing ||(A^0)^{-1}E_sigma|| small, and the split A^0 = A^c + B^im + E, are not justified near the arc endpoints. The Neumann-series arguments in the nearest-image and computable theorems rely on this.
issues.title: Exponential smallness of E_sigma on Y_R justified by a result that explicitly does not cover Gamma_R x Gamma_R
issues.why_classification: Fixing the cutoff and adding a direct kernel estimate is a short, routine repair that keeps the method and all claimed rates.

issues.failure_explanation: The physical solution u is not close to the PML solution in the PML layer. There u_sigma approximates the complex-scaled continuation u(F_sigma(x)), which is exponentially damped, whereas u itself is not small. So ||u - u_sigma^ni||_{H^1(K)} and ||u - u_sigma^c||_{H^1(K)} cannot be exponentially small for K meeting Omega_R minus Omega_p. The proofs invoke Theorem exact-conv and eq. (pde-conv), which are proved only for K inside Omega_p. Theorem thm:computable-convergence repeats the same K in Omega_R.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace K in Omega_R by K in Omega_p in both statements, matching the PDE theorem on which the proofs rely.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, the field-convergence conclusions of the nearest-image and computable theorems are false on the PML part of Omega_R. They are supported only on compact subsets of the physical region.
issues.title: Field-error estimates stated on compact K in Omega_R, but u differs from the PML solution inside the PML
issues.why_classification: The proofs already work on Omega_p, so the fix is a one-word change to the domain with no loss of the intended physical-region result.

issues.failure_explanation: The flat model operator L_{sigma,t} has no alpha_2 and its fields live on the unbounded quarter-plane. The true operator L_sigma on Omega_R^± has A_sigma = diag(alpha_2/alpha_1, alpha_1/alpha_2) and J = alpha_1 alpha_2. It therefore differs from L_{sigma,t} for |x_2| > L_2, and the box has Neumann boundaries at x_2 = ±(L_2+d_2). Since L_sigma U_{sigma,t} is not zero there, the commutator identity gives L_sigma(eta U_t) = alpha_1^{-1}(eta'' U_t + 2 eta' d_s U_t) only when coefficients are the same. So W = U_sigma - eta U_t does not satisfy the stated equations (QBim-W-PDE) with source supported only in C_b^±. There are extra residuals, (L_sigma - L_{sigma,t})(eta U_t) in the vertical PML and a non-zero conormal on the top and bottom boundaries. These are not exponentially small: at tangential frequency 0 the model solution decays like e^{(tau/alpha_1)n} with tau/alpha_1 = -ik, so there is no attenuation in n. They are never estimated, so (QBim-correction-by-U) is unproved.
